incident_triage.title: Production incident triage

ticket.customer_message: Checkout has been failing for most of our customers since about 9:10 this morning. We are seeing 500 errors on every region we tried. We have orders waiting and no workaround. Please get someone on this now.
ticket.recent_change: A payment-service deployment completed at 09:05 local time.
ticket.routing_policy: Route software failures and outages to Technical Support; payment settlement and invoice questions to Billing; plan changes and pre-sales questions to Accounts.
ticket.escalation_policy: Page the on-call engineer for a production outage affecting multiple regions or most customers when no workaround is available. Do not page for an isolated user issue or a question that has a working workaround.

team.instructions: Which team should own this ticket under the routing policy?

criteria.technical_support: Software failures, integrations, and service outages
criteria.accounts: Plan changes, account setup, and pre-sales questions

customer_impact.instructions: How much customer impact does the incident report describe?
criteria: One customer or an isolated request is affected
A limited group has degraded service
Most customers cannot complete a production workflow

page_on_call.instructions: Under the escalation policy, should the on-call engineer be paged now?

criteria.true: A multi-region or broad production outage has no known workaround
criteria.false: The report describes a limited issue or a working workaround

customer_frustration.instructions: How frustrated does the customer sound in the message?
criteria: Clearly frustrated and asking for urgent help

incident_triage.hint: This uses one realistic incident for four focused decisions: route, impact, escalation, and tone. Jev answers them together; application code can combine the typed answers and confidence into its own workflow. Change the incident details to see which decisions move.
